PCI.BIO: Jorge Castillo, Ph.D. is an Assistant Professor in Cybersecurity at The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley. Dr. Castillo is a researcher specializing in the fields of Blockchain, Machine Learning, and IoT. His focus is on developing security-oriented applications to improve and promote privacy in different industrial domains.

CONGRANT.TITLE: NexGenPOST2 Phase II: Verified Onboard Bearing and Wheel Condition Monitoring with Cybersecurity and Workforce Development
Equipping undergraduates with computational engineering skills for the challenges of tomorrow through project-based learning
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The proposed project seeks to enhance undergraduate STEM education at UTRGV by strengthening computationally intensive courses such as Computational Fluid Dynamics, Blockchain, Machine Learning, Finite Element Analysis, Senior Design, and Undergraduate Research. Through the acquisition of a dedicated computer cluster, the project will provide students with the necessary resources to perform large-scale simulations and data-intensive tasks that are currently impractical, thereby improving the learning experience.

CONGRANT.TITLE: AI-Bridge: Bridging AI Accessibility Through Open-source Solutions
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The project aims to enhance AI adoption by developing open-source, user-friendly tools and secure frameworks that lower technical barriers for students and researchers. At the same time, it seeks to expand AI accessibility within educational programs by strengthening coursework, hands-on training, and outreach initiatives. Through the use of portable AI devices, students will be able to engage in small-scale AI projects more easily, without relying on high-performance GPU servers, thereby fostering broader AI literacy and practical experience.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Privacy-Preserving Medical LLMs: Federated Learning with Robust Aggregation Guided by Large-Scale Evaluation
CONGRANT.SPONORG: Texas Academy of Medicine, Engineering, Science and Technology
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The project aims to develop a federated learning (FL) framework tailored for distributed medical data that preserves privacy while supporting multi-modal integration. It will design efficient aggregation strategies to manage noisy, heterogeneous, and potentially adversarial client updates, and incorporate a large-scale supernet model as a meta-evaluator, leveraging knowledge distillation to improve model performance, fairness, and explanation quality. Ultimately, the project seeks to deliver a scalable and transferable framework that can serve as a model for secure and trustworthy medical AI deployment across diverse healthcare systems.

CONGRANT.TITLE: TX-CIPHER: Texas Cybersecurity Introduction Program for High-school Education and Readiness
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The program seeks to develop participants’ critical thinking, problem-solving, and ethical decision-making skills in cybersecurity through hands-on activities, while also building a mentorship structure that cultivates leadership among undergraduate mentors. Collectively, these efforts will strengthen practical cybersecurity skills, expand the cybersecurity education workforce, and establish a scalable outreach model with best practices that can be replicated at other institutions.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Identifying the role of HIV-1 infection in the brain with Alzheimer’s Disease
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: This project investigates the role of IFIT3 and STAT1 genes in neuroinflammation associated with HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). In humanized mouse models, the project will examine how HIV-1 infection alters IFIT3 and STAT1 expression and impacts the Jak/STAT signaling pathway in HAND. In mouse models, the project will characterize the contribution of these genes to amyloid-beta–induced neuroinflammation in AD. Finally, analyses of archived human brain tissues from HAND and AD patients will assess genomic and proteomic changes in IFIT3 and STAT1, providing insight into their regulatory roles in neuroinflammation and their combined contribution to HAND and AD pathologies.

CONGRANT.TITLE: SHELTER (Security Hub for Enhanced Learning, Threat Evaluation, and Resilience) Cybersecurity Clinic
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: SHELTER seeks to promote the success of minority students in cybersecurity by fostering an inclusive and supportive environment, while bridging classroom learning with real-world applications to strengthen career readiness. The program aims to raise awareness of cybersecurity risks and cultivate a proactive security culture, equip participants with both theoretical knowledge and hands-on training to develop practical skills, and establish effective incident response plans to reduce the impact of cybersecurity incidents and enhance organizational resilience.​​​​

INTELLCONT.TITLE: MedBlockSync: A blockchain Solution for Multi-Institutional Healthcare

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas at San Antonio

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The integration of Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) into the healthcare industry has revolutionized patient data management by enabling the storage of highly sensitive information. However, the continuous exchange of this information among health institutions to ensure accurate patient care introduces significant challenges related to data dissemination and security. Blockchain technology, with its inherent properties of decentralization, immutability, and transparency, offers a robust solution to these challenges, facilitating secure and efficient data sharing among stakeholders. In this paper, we present MedBlockSync, a robust blockchain system designed for improved data integrity across multi-institutional healthcare organizations. The framework is developed to achieve three key objectives: (1) safeguarding EMR data against cyberattacks, (2) enabling seamless and secure sharing of healthcare information among various stakeholders, and (3) facilitating Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) communication, including real-time data transmission from smart sensors to the blockchain network and EMRs through a secure channel. By incorporating advanced security features into EMRs without necessitating modifications to existing digital health infrastructures, MedBlockSync enhances interoperability among healthcare systems, ensuring both scalability and adaptability in the digital health landscape.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: The Weaving of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence into the Fabric of Cybersecurity Curriculum: From Degree Plans to Capstone Projects
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
Abstract
As our newly designed degree in Cybersecurity enters its fourth year, students in the program are starting to take courses beyond the basic ones, including senior courses, technical electives, and capstone projects. While Cybersecurity is at the heart of our degree that addresses the national need for cybersecurity specialists, how we approach the education and pedagogy of cybersecurity in the era of Big Data and AI/ML (Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning) is a question that we are addressing in real-time as techniques and measures and countermeasures of cybersecurity attacks keep evolving and taking advantages of the rapid advancements in computing, memory, storage, networking, and virtualization technologies.

Educational modules with hands-on labs are available at different junctions to give students in the program multiple chances to incorporate the latest techniques in AI/ML into their degree. Whether it is advising and orientation sessions, faculty-led seminars, student-club workshops, technical electives, or capstone projects, custom-tailored material has been created specifically for our cybersecurity students. This paper presents our systematic efforts to pervade the curriculum with a hands-on, immersive approach to integrating AI/ML. We will present the following modules that were developed or are currently being developed.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: DPT Attack: Abusing Differential Privacy Triggers to Improve Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for decentralized model training, offering privacy-preserving benefits. However, it is vulnerable to backdoor attacks, which exploit its decentralized nature. This study introduces the Differential Privacy-based Trigger (DPT) attack, a new approach to injecting backdoors by leveraging differential privacy mechanisms. Using publicly available datasets (MNIST, Fashion MNIST, and CIFAR10), we evaluate DPT’s impact on backdoor effectiveness, evasiveness, and model utility, comparing it with conventional color trigger (CT) patterns. Our findings reveal that DPT attacks achieve higher evasiveness and effectiveness, bypassing state-of-the-art defenses in different adversarial configurations, including constrain-and-scale and multiple backdoor attacks. The results highlight significant vulnerabilities in FL systems when differential privacy is incorporated, underscoring the need for robust mitigation strategies.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: MIND-IoT: Machine Intelligence and Data-Mining for IoT Threats

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The use of electric motors drive numerous industries via robust mechanical and electromechanical systems. However, their ubiquitous presence across the industry makes them potential targets for cyber-attackers, raising serious privacy concerns. Prior studies have demonstrated the feasibility of accurately fingerprinting various devices using electromagnetic signals. Yet, the specialized equipment required for those methods remain complex and expensive. This study presents MIND-IoT, a novel approach that captures and analyzes the unintended magnetic emissions surrounding electric motors. Our method achieves precise fingerprinting of motors, and determines their operational parameters by leveraging low-cost IoT devices. By focusing solely on magnetic fields, MIND-IoT offers a cost-effective fingerprinting solution while highlighting the urgent need to address associated privacy risks.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: MediLink: A Secure Blockchain Framework for Multi-Institutional Healthcare

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas at San Antonio

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The use of Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) in the healthcare industry has proven to be critical for storing highly sensitive information. Disseminating and protecting healthcare data poses major challenges for the current healthcare information system. Blockchain technology provides solutions to these challenges with its inherited properties, such as decentralization, immutability, and transparency. This provides a unique opportunity to improve data sharing among stakeholders. We propose MediLink, a blockchain-based framework for secure collaborative medical storage. MediLink is designed to (1) protect EMR data from cyber attacks, (2) share healthcare information of patients with different stakeholders, and (3) enable the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) (e.g., smart sensors) communication and real-time data transmission with EMR and the blockchain network through a secured channel. MediLink adds security features to EMRs without requiring modification of current digital health infrastructures, increasing interoperability among healthcare systems.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: The TLB Mage: On How Modern TLB Designs Accelerate PTE-based Cache Side-channel Attacks

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas at San Antonio
The University of Texas at San Antonio
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas at San Antonio

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
Previously proposed Xlate attacks demonstrate how a devoted adversary can mount an indirect cache side-channel attack by manipulating the memory management unit (MMU) implemented in recent Intel processors. While Xlate attacks are overall hard to mitigate, these require the adversary to constantly clean the translation lookaside buffer (TLB), an internal component in the MMU that stores recently-used page-table entries (PTEs). Doing so requires the adversary to perform numerous memory accesses, which in turn takes a considerable amount of time, and as a result, this makes Xlate attacks significantly slower when compared to other cache side-channel techniques.
In this work, however, we demonstrate how an adversary can significantly speedup the TLB cleaning process to carry out swift Xlate attacks. This is possible because, in reality, it is not necessary to clean the entire TLB to effectively carry out Xlate, but only specific portions of the internal TLB structure. Based on this, the TLB Mage leads to faster and more effective Xlate attacks by automatically indicating to the adversary what specific portions of the TLB require cleaning. In practice, when targeting an Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) cipher with an Xlate cache side-channel attack, the TLB Mage leads to attacks 1.72 times faster than the baseline Xlate attack sequence from the literature.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: FLEDGE: Ledger-based Federated Learning Resilient to Inference and Backdoor Attacks

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: University of Texas at San Antonio

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed learning process that uses a trusted aggregation server to allow multiple parties (or clients) to collaboratively train a machine learning model without having them share their private data. Recent research, however, has demonstrated the effectiveness of inference and poisoning attacks on FL. Mitigating both attacks simultaneously is very challenging. State-of-the-art solutions have proposed the use of poisoning defenses with Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) and/or Differential Privacy (DP). However, these techniques are not efficient and fail to address the malicious intent behind the attacks, i.e., adversaries (curious servers and/or compromised clients) seek to exploit a system for monetization purposes. To overcome these limitations, we present a ledger-based FL framework known as FLEDGE that allows making parties accountable for their behavior and achieve reasonable efficiency for mitigating inference and poisoning attacks. Our solution leverages crypto-currency to increase party accountability by penalizing malicious behavior and rewarding benign conduct. We conduct an extensive evaluation on four public datasets: Reddit, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10. Our experimental results demonstrate that (1) FLEDGE provides strong privacy guarantees for model updates without sacrificing model utility; (2) FLEDGE can successfully mitigate different poisoning attacks without degrading the performance of the global model; and (3) FLEDGE offers unique reward mechanisms to promote benign behavior during model training and/or model aggregation.
